channel.title: Daily World Bulletin

item.title: Indian cargo ship sinks off Yemen coast, crew rescued
item.description: An Indian-flagged cargo vessel sank off the coast of Yemen in the Red Sea following a projectile attack. Reports indicate that either 13 or 14 Indian sailors were aboard the ship during the incident and all have been safely rescued. The attack in Yemeni waters comes amid broader regional maritime security concerns and fluctuating global oil prices. Further official details regarding the nature of the projectile and the identity of the vessel remain limited.

item.title: Trump Warns Iran Over Hormuz Strait As Oil Prices Drop
item.description: United States President Donald Trump stated that Iran will face severe consequences if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened soon. Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed that discussions have advanced to help resume oil shipments. These developments coincide with a fall in global oil prices. Further official updates regarding the maritime route and diplomatic talks are awaited as authorities monitor the situation closely.

item.title: How single people are teaming up to cut rising living costs
item.description: Single individuals frequently encounter higher expenses for housing, utility bills, groceries, and vacations compared to couples or families. By pooling resources and living arrangements, singles are finding practical ways to manage their expenses and ease the economic impact of living alone. Details regarding specific financial strategies remain limited in the current report, but cooperative living is emerging as a popular solution.

item.title: Parliamentary Panel Threatens Meta With Safe Harbour Withdrawal
item.description: A parliamentary committee has directed Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to issue an apology within three months regarding the removal of the Prime Minister's speech from Facebook and wrongful account actions. The panel has threatened to strip the tech giant of its legal safe harbour immunity if it fails to comply. Additionally, the government intends to question Meta executives regarding child sexual abuse material lapses and artificial intelligence-generated content when a global team visits India in August.

item.description: A recent Russian military strike resulted in the deaths of at least 17 people. The announcements provided new financial insights into the aerospace manufacturer, leading to immediate market reactions regarding its heavy capital allocation toward artificial intelligence development.

item.title: India include four net bowlers for Sri Lanka Tests
item.description: Ahead of the upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka, the Indian team has summoned four spin bowlers to assist with practice sessions in the nets. item.title: Madhavan's biopic universe expands with G.D.N and Rocketry
item.description: Actor R Madhavan's biopic universe is expanding, centering around projects like Rocketry and the upcoming film G.D.N, which explores the life of the inventor often called the Edison of India. Makers recently revealed actor Vinay Rai's look as Bhupendra in the movie. Reports highlight how Madhavan prepared for the role using rare videos and audiobooks. The film is scheduled for release on August 7, shining a light on India's unsung historical heroes and adding to the actor's growing cinematic footprint.

item.title: Bird flu threatens nearly 400 Australian species including penguins and dolphins
item.description: Recent reports reveal that nearly 400 Australian species, including little penguins and dolphins, face significant threats from bird flu. Australia has confirmed its first mass wildlife mortality linked to the virus. Authorities warn that H5N1 detections continue to rise and the disease is likely to spread further across the region. Experts estimate that specific local penguin colonies could potentially lose up to forty percent of their population. Officials and researchers are closely monitoring the situation as the true extent of the ecological disaster unfolds.

item.title: NASA and SpaceX to Observe Rocket Stage Lunar Impact
item.description: NASA and SpaceX are actively tracking a used Falcon 9 upper stage from a commercial mission that is expected to impact the Moon near the Einstein and Bell craters. Researchers plan to use various ground-based telescopes and space-based assets to observe the event and collect valuable lunar data. Officials have confirmed that the upcoming impact poses no danger to Earth. Details regarding the exact scientific measurements and instruments being deployed for this observation campaign remain limited.

item.description: The Supreme Court has observed that listening to the youth is the most powerful force for preventing protest violence, advising authorities to engage with Gen Z rather than repressing them. Amid recent NEET-UG protests, the apex court emphasized that counselling and pacification, combined with restraint from law enforcement, serve as a much better response to student demonstrators than aggression. These observations emerged alongside related legal petitions regarding recent demonstration management.

item.title: Centre Tightens Surveillance on GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs and Bans Surrogate Promotion

The administration also stated an ambitious target to achieve a $1.5 trillion economy by the year 2031, while asserting strict financial accountability measures.

Authorities are examining the circumstances surrounding the marketing controversy, which sparked public backlash. Further details regarding the ongoing police inquiries remain limited at this stage.

item.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 13: Opposition Protests Continue

Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi led a demonstration near the Prime Minister's residence, demanding resignations from the Prime Minister and the Home Minister. The Lok Sabha faced adjournment until two in the afternoon. With the opposition hardening its stance, reports indicate a complete washout of the session is likely.
